title: POC: Credential Sprint & Environment Readiness Review
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on credential handoff, network readiness, and a brief readout of early latency/throughput numbers. Agreed on next steps for KMS integration, service account rotation, and a constrained benchmark run on staging with pinned model config.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-29 15:00 PT | Duration: ~46m | Recording ID: ff-20260629-velora-001
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Velora), Priya Rao (Velora), Jonas Lee (Velora)

[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining. good to see you all. quick check — is this still a hard 46 min block?
[00:06] Carlos: yes that's perfect, we have a quick stand after so we're tight.
[00:12] Maya: cool i'll keep this tight. objective today: credential sprint status, network/gateway readiness, and a short pass on the staging bench results. Ethan will do the perf readout.
[00:20] Ethan: hi all, i'll try to surface the numbers and then we can dig into access bits. there may be a couple transcription hiccups — i talked about K-V cash in the doc, that's KV cache not cash.
[00:30] Priya: haha noted. quick note: our infra team rotated the test creds last night; we pushed a new service account but we haven't yet attached the role for cross-account STS.
[00:40] Jonas: and i opened the ticket for SAML mapping, still waiting on our identity team to confirm the attribute mapping.

[00:55] Ethan: ok on the bench: we ran a constrained shadow-run against the Redwood hosted endpoint with a 4k token seq, batch size 8 at peak. median latency for a 512-token chunk was ~170ms, 95th around 420ms. cost per 1k tokens estimated slightly higher than our prediction because we didn't have prefix caching enabled.
[01:20] Carlos: hm 420ms 95th — that's higher than we hoped. was that with quantized model or FP16?
[01:25] Ethan: that run was FP16 on dedupe variant. we also tried an int8-lite quantized path but realized our quant pipeline wasn't set right; the model fell back to full precision on some sequences.
[01:40] Maya: can you drop the raw CSV to the shared drive after? we'll annotate the scenarios.
[01:46] Ethan: sure will do. link: google.com/drive/fake-bench (placeholder in transcript)

[02:00] Priya: back to creds: we looked at the KMS flow — Velora uses an HSM-backed KMS. we need the Redwood side to accept customer-managed keys for the pilot, is that supported?
[02:12] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we support BYOK and customer-managed KMS. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption and integrate with an external KMS via a connector, but that requires an IR (integration runbook) and a short security review.
[02:30] Carlos: would that add lead time? our compliance window is two weeks.
[02:35] Ethan: realistically the KMS connector and key rotation automation is about 5-7 business days if we have final DNS and the KMS admin grant. but for the pilot we can do a temporary sealed-secret flow — not ideal but short-term.

[03:00] Jonas: network question — do you require VPC peering or can we use PrivateLink / transit gateway? our security prefers no peering with third-party infra.
[03:10] Maya: we support both. Redwood Dedicated or Private uses VPC peering for lowest latency, but we can do AWS PrivateLink or Azure Private Endpoint for hosted integration; there are tradeoffs on egress and NAT.
[03:30] Priya: what about egress rules and egress IPs? we need static egress for our firewall policy.
[03:36] Ethan: we can provide a set of egress IPs for the gateway but if you need strict source IPs for the service worker nodes that requires dedicated capacity or Private deployment.

[03:55] Carlos: okay good. action on our side: i'll confirm if static egress is mandatory for the pilot.
[04:05] Maya: perfect.

[04:18] Ethan: quick note on KV cache: enabling prefix cache dropped token volume by about 22% in our internal traces. if you can share representative prompts we can add them to the prefix set and likely cut cost.
[04:32] Carlos: we'll extract a sample of top 50 prompt prefixes and share.

[04:45] Jonas: one more thing — telemetry. we need structured traces sent to our datadog and we also want request-level IDs to match logs. can you push headers through?
[04:55] Ethan: yes the SDK supports X-Request-ID and we have a trace hook for Datadog. will need a small env var to flip on in staging.

[05:10] Maya: going to the timeline: remaining items in the sprint — Priya to finish STS role, Carlos to provide prefix sample and bench scenarios, Redwood to run a pinned-run with caching on staging, and an encrypted key handoff path for KMS evaluation.

[05:28] Priya: on STS — we have a temporary policy that allows assume-role for the Redwood service account but we want the rotation window to be 24 hours, can you support that?
[05:36] Ethan: our rotation tooling supports 1h-30d windows, 24h is fine. need the role ARN and the trust policy.

[05:52] Maya: cool. i'm going to flag a subtle item — we've seen some customers hit rate-limiting because autoscaling had a conservative ramp. if your pilot has spikes please tell us and we'll bump the burst limits for the POC.
[06:05] Carlos: expected spikes when batch jobs run — likely around 11am UTC next Tuesday.
[06:12] Maya: noted. we'll provision burst capacity for that window.

[06:25] Ethan: small perf detail — when sequence lengths vary a lot, the scheduler will sometimes underutilize the GPU due to dynamic batching. we have a knob — max-seq-window — that can be tuned. we suggested 2048 for your average traffic but if you have many short queries it should be lower.
[06:44] Carlos: our production mix is mostly 64-512 tokens with occasional 2k requests for long-form.
[06:50] Ethan: ok keep it at 1024 then, we'll try that for the next run.

[07:02] Jonas: curious about observability retention — are logs kept by default? we need audit logs for 90 days.
[07:10] Maya: hosted has 30 days default, enterprise add-on can extend. for Private, retention is customer-controlled. we can surface a pricing line for 90d retention.

[07:25] Carlos: that's fine as an add-on for now, but we need to know pricing.

[07:35] Maya: noted, we'll include the retention pricing in the follow-up packet.

[07:45] Ethan: quick thing i ran into — the staging run had S3 access errors for model shards when we tried the quant pipeline. looks like role permission for the shard bucket is missing read:s3:GetObject for the staging worker role.
[07:58] Priya: ah we missed the policy. i'll add the GetObject on the model shard bucket and push.
[08:05] Ethan: great, that should let the quant job run. once quant runs we can compare the int8-lite path and report accuracy delta.

[08:20] Maya: any compliance blockers? I know Velora is PCI-adjacent and may need PCI scoping for production later.
[08:28] Carlos: for POC we don't expect full PCI but we need assurance that tokens are not logged and that we have an exportable audit trail.
[08:36] Maya: yes by default we can disable logging of user payloads and add request-retention policies; we'll also share the SOC2 snapshot.

[08:46] Jonas: on success criteria — for the pilot we want 95th latency under 500ms for our 64-512 mix, cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll supply target), and a vetted key rotation workflow.
[08:59] Maya: sounds reasonable. we'll validate next run against that.

[09:10] Ethan: ok i will schedule two bench runs: one with prefix caching enabled and max-seq-window 1024, and one replicating your production mix with spikes; will post CSV and annotated notes.

[09:25] Priya: and on the SSO mapping — we will need a sample SAML metadata file and the attribute mapping. Jonas will own that.
[09:33] Jonas: got it.

[09:40] Maya: time check — 40 minutes in. quick recap and owners?
[09:45] Carlos: go ahead maya.
[09:46] Maya: Ok recap: Redwood runs pinned staging bench with caching on Thurs, Ethan posts results and CSV; Priya finishes role policy and adds S3 GetObject for model shards by EOD tomorrow; Carlos sends top-50 prefix set and cost target by Friday; Jonas provides SAML metadata; Redwood sends KMS integration runbook and retention pricing.
[10:08] Carlos: all good. couple clarifications — when you say "pinned run" can you confirm model hash/variant?
[10:15] Ethan: yes i'll include model id and quant profile in the CSV.

[10:22] Maya: any blockers not listed?
[10:24] Priya: none from infra once i update the policy.
[10:27] Jonas: none from product.

[10:30] Maya: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email with links and action items.
[10:36] Carlos: thanks, appreciate the quick sync.
[10:40] Maya: bye all.

[END]
